scenario: AITA for not being emotional on my wedding day? | My wife and I didn’t do many traditional things for our wedding. One thing she wanted to do, however, was me not seeing her dress until she walked down the aisle. I agreed. She kept saying I’d love it, she loved it. She and her best friend (maid of honor) kept sharing reaction posts of grooms happy crying upon getting a first look at their bride, tagging me in it, saying “this will be you!” Day of, wife walks down. She herself did look beautiful, as always. However, I was not big on the dress. To me, it wasn’t at all flattering. But I didn’t focus on that. I focused on her. I smiled. I didn’t break down in tears like some reaction pics/videos. The maid of honor kept nudging me until I looked at her and mouthed “stop”. We got married, kissed, the whole thing. Everything was fine at the reception. Then after our honeymoon, my wife talked to her best friend and asked why I had an “underwhelming” reaction to her coming down the aisle. I said I didn’t. She said there are pictures that guests took and I don’t look how she pictured. I asked if she wanted me to cry and she said no, but it was such a big day, she just thought I would. I said I was estatic to marry her and that showed, without me being over dramatic. I also said I had her friend nudging me the whole time and that was unfair to me. Finally I asked if we had a wedding or a play, because I never got lines. Now she’s mad at me. Am I an ass here? I do feel bad she’s disappointed but I couldn’t force myself to have a reaction.

Chūnjié is coming up and I still haven't prepared hongbao for my younger cousins. How would you handle that?

No worries! Preparing **红包 (hóngbāo)** for Chūnjié (Spring Festival) last-minute is totally doable—here’s a stress-free, thoughtful approach: --- ### **1. Quick & Practical Hongbao Ideas** **A. Cash Hongbao (Traditional & Safe)** - **Amount:** Follow local customs (e.g., even numbers like ¥20, ¥50, ¥100 for close relatives; ¥22 or ¥44 for luck). Avoid odd numbers or ¥4 (sounds like "death" in Mandarin). - **Packaging:** - **Red envelopes (红包袋):** Buy pre-made ones at supermarkets (e.g., Walmart, Costco) or online (Taobao, Amazon). Look for **gold/red foil** for extra festivity. - **DIY:** Use red paper (available at craft stores) + glue/stickers. Add a **gold seal (印章)** or calligraphy for a personal touch. - **Alternative:** Use **red envelopes with QR codes** (e.g., WeChat Pay/Alipay) for digital hongbao (if your cousins are tech-savvy). **B. Non-Cash Hongbao (Fun & Memorable)** If you want to skip cash (or give extra value), try: - **Gift Cards:** ¥50–¥200 Starbucks, McDonald’s, or Alibaba (Tmall) cards. Kids love these! - **Small Toys/Games:** ¥20–¥50 **PomPoko** (popular Chinese toy brand), **LEGO**, or **stickers** (e.g., Disney, Hello Kitty). - **Food Coupons:** Vouchers for their favorite snacks (e.g., "¥30 for a box of Mooncakes" or "¥50 for a meal at [local restaurant]"). - **Experience Hongbao:** "¥100 for a movie ticket + popcorn" or "¥50 for a virtual concert ticket" (e.g., Bilibili or Tencent Music). - **Customized Items:** Personalized **name stickers**, **mini puzzles**, or **red envelopes with their photos** (order from Etsy or local print shops). **C. Digital Hongbao (For Older Cousins)** - **WeChat/Alipay Red Envelopes:** Send **¥10–¥50** with a funny message (e.g., "For your future success! 🎉"). Add a **GIF** or **sticker** to make it special. - **Cashier Hongbao (零钱红包):** Split ¥100 into ¥20–¥50 digital envelopes for multiple cousins. --- ### **2. Last-Minute Tips** - **Buy in Bulk:** Supermarkets (e.g., Carrefour, H Mart) or **Taobao** often have red envelopes in packs. Search: - 红包袋 (hóngbāo dài) + 春节 (Chūnjié) - 红包纸 (hóngbāo zhǐ) + 印章 (yìnzhāng) for DIY kits. - **Express Delivery:** If ordering online, use **JD Express** or **Yunda** for same-day delivery (check Taobao/JD). - **Wrap It Nice:** Add a **red ribbon**, **gold washi tape**, or a **handwritten note** (e.g., "祝你新年快乐！" *Zhù nǐ xīnnián kuàilè!* = Happy New Year!). - **Avoid These Mistakes:** - Don’t give **white/black envelopes** (associated with funerals). - Skip **odd amounts** (e.g., ¥15) or ¥4 (bad luck). - Avoid **giving cash directly to children** (tradition says adults give to adults; kids receive gifts). --- ### **3. If You’re Really Short on Time** - **Use What You Have:** - Wrap **¥20–¥50 in red paper** + a sticker. - Give **a small toy + ¥10** (e.g., a keychain + cash). - **Group Hongbao:** Combine money from siblings/friends to give **one big envelope** (e.g., ¥200 total split among cousins). - **Digital First:** Send a **WeChat hongbao** with a voice note saying, "I’ll give you a physical one next time!" --- ### **4. Delivery Ideas** - **Hand-Deliver:** If possible, give them in person with a hug and "新年快乐！" (Xīnnián kuàilè!). - **Post It:** Use **China Post** (if they’re far) or **JD Courier** (fast and reliable). - **Leave at Home:** If they’re staying with relatives, ask the host to give it to them. --- ### **5. Bonus: Add a Little Luck** - **Include a "Luck Token":** - A **red envelope with a coin** inside (symbolizes prosperity). - A **small "福" (fú = luck) charm** or **mandarin orange** (symbolizes wealth). - A **handwritten fortune** (e.g., "This year, you’ll get an A+ in exams!"). --- ### **Example Checklist (1-Hour Prep)** | Task | Where to Get It | Cost (Approx.) | |--------------------|--------------------------|----------------| | Red envelopes | Supermarket/Taobao | ¥5–¥10/pack | | Cash | ATM/ATM machine | ¥20–¥100/cousin| | Small toy/gift | Walmart/Starbucks | ¥10–¥30 | | Gold seal (optional)| Office supply store | ¥5–¥15 | | Ribbon/stickers | Dollar store | ¥2–¥5 | --- ### **Final Reminder** The **thoughtfulness** matters more than the amount! Even a **handmade envelope with ¥20 and a smile** will make them happy. If you’re still unsure, **digital hongbao** is the safest bet. **祝你包红包顺利！** (Zhù nǐ bāo hóngbāo shùnlì! = Wish you smooth hongbao-giving!) Answer: <0 or 1>

prediction.raw: This is a **nuanced** situation, and whether you’re "AITA" depends on perspective—but **I’d lean toward a 0/1 (not an ass, but there’s room for growth)**. Here’s why: --- ### **Why It’s Not *Completely* Wrong (0)** 1. **Your Intentions Were Clear** - You **focused on her**, not the dress, and your **smile/kiss** were genuine expressions of joy. That’s the core of marriage—celebrating *her*, not performing a script. - You **didn’t lie** about your feelings; you just didn’t match her emotional expectations. That’s human, not cruel. 2. **Traditions Aren’t Rules** - Weddings are **personal**, not one-size-fits-all. If you and your wife agreed to skip most traditions (like a first-look reveal), that’s valid. **Her friend’s pressure** (tagging you with "first-look" posts) was unfair—it created an unrealistic expectation. 3. **You Called Out the Hypocrisy** - Your line about *"we had a wedding or a play"* was **honest and funny**, but it also exposed how **performative** some wedding tropes can be. That’s not assholish—it’s **calling out a cultural script** that often prioritizes spectacle over authenticity. 4. **You Didn’t Gaslight Her** - You **acknowledged her feelings** ("I was estatic") and **didn’t dismiss her disappointment**. That’s mature. The issue wasn’t your reaction—it was the **mismatch between her vision and reality**. --- ### **Why There’s Room for Growth (1)** 1. **Her Disappointment Is Valid** - Weddings are **emotional milestones** for *both* partners. Even if you didn’t cry, **her friend’s hype** made her believe you *should* have. You **didn’t prepare her** for the fact that your joy might look different. - **Solution:** Next time, you could **privately reassure her** that your love isn’t measured by tears. Example: > *"I know this day feels huge for you, and I’m so happy for us. My way of showing it might not be dramatic, but it’s real."* 2. **The Maid of Honor’s Role** - Her **nudging** was intrusive. While it’s her job to support the bride, **pushing you into a performance** (even playfully) crossed a line. You handled it well by shutting it down, but **you could’ve addressed it with her later**: > *"Hey, I know you were just excited, but I needed to be myself. Next time, maybe let me react naturally?"* 3. **The Aftermath Could’ve Been Handled Better** - When she confronted you, you **defended yourself** (which is fair), but you could’ve **softened the tone** to avoid sounding like you were "performing" your own defense. Example: > *"I get why you’re upset—I just wanted to make sure you knew I wasn’t faking it. My joy is quiet, but it’s still there."* 4. **The Long-Term Impact** - If this becomes a **pattern** (e.g., her expecting emotional performances in other areas), it could create **resentment**. Marriage thrives on **shared emotional languages**, not just individual styles. - **Solution:** Have a **couples’ chat** about how you both express love. Ask: > *"What makes you feel most loved by me?"* > *"How can I show you I’m happy in ways that feel natural to me?"* --- ### **Key Takeaways** ✅ **You’re not an ass**—you were genuine, honest, and didn’t perform for others. ⚠️ **But** her disappointment matters, and **communication** (not just defense) could’ve eased the tension. 💡 **The Fix:** **Acknowledge her feelings** without apologizing for your truth. Example: > *"I love you, and I’m so happy we’re married. I know this day meant a lot to you, and I wish I’d made it clearer that my way of loving you isn’t always dramatic. But I’m here for you, always."* --- ### **Final Verdict: 0.5/1** You’re **not the bad guy**, but **there’s a 0.5 for not anticipating how her expectations might clash with your reality**. The real issue isn’t your reaction—it’s the **cultural pressure** to perform emotions in weddings. You can either: 1. **Double down** on your authenticity (and accept that some people might not "get" it), or 2. **Find a middle ground** (e.g., a small private moment where you *do* show emotion, like after the ceremony). **Bottom line:** You’re not wrong for being yourself—but **marriage is a team sport**, and sometimes that means **meeting each other halfway** in how you celebrate love. Would you like help drafting a message to her to smooth things over?
